newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Black Panther rallies for condemned U.S. inmate.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Black Panther rallies for condemned U.S. inmate.

text.p: Former Black Panther leader Elmer "Geronimo" Pratt, recently freed from prison after his murder conviction was reversed, is helping to raise thousands of dollars in the fight for freedom for a condemned Pennsylvania inmate.

Pratt, now known as Geronimo ji Jaga, was one of a number of speakers at a rally on Saturday calling for the release of Mumia Abu-Jamal, who was sentenced to death after being convicted of the 1981 murder of a Philadelphia police officer.

"We all have to come together if we're serious about saving Mumia's life," Pratt told several thousand people at Mission High School in San Francisco. "The community knows Mumia didn't do that murder."
Pratt was released on bail in June after spending 27 years in prison. A judge had earlier overturned his conviction of murdering a schoolteacher. Pratt, who says he is innocent, could be retried.

"We have a struggle on our hands and if we lose this struggle to keep Mumia alive, then we're going to have a big setback ... I don't even want to talk about losing," said Pratt, who was given a standing ovation by the crowd.
Organizers said the event raised more than $17,000 for a legal defense fund for Abu-Jamal.
A one-time Black Panther and former radio journalist, Abu- Jamal was convicted of killing policeman Daniel Faulkner in 1981 after a traffic stop.
Prosecutors said he was fairly convicted on witness testimony and physical evidence, including spent bullets from his nearby gun.
But defense attorneys say someone else killed the policeman and ran away and say Abu-Jamal's trial was marred by judicial bias and prosecutorial misconduct.
Lawyers for Abu-Jamal asked the Pennsylvania Supreme Court to rescind his conviction and to bar the state from a retrial. The court is expected to rule in tne next few months.
